newsitem.title: USA: Medtronic says Hemopump in Phase II trials.
newsitem.headline: Medtronic says Hemopump in Phase II trials.

text.p: Medtronic Inc said Phase II clinical trials began with a new medical device expected to cut hospitalization time for patients who undergo minimally invasive heart surgery.

The Medtronic Hemopump Cardiac Assist System was used by surgeon Dr. Robert Matheny at the Indiana Heart Institute Hospital in Indianapolis to support a patient undergoing a multi-vessel coronary bypass procedure, Medtronic said.

"This operation, in which the Hemopump system completely replaced a conventional 'heart/lung machine,' was the first in the United States since the system was acquired by Medtronic, said the medical devices manufacturer.

The Hemopump improves cardiac output for patients during minimally invasive coronary bypass surgery and for other situations in which the heart must be relieved of some of its pumping load, Medtronic said.
The device's pump assembly is positioned to speed blood movement from the left ventricle of the slowed heart into the ascending aorta, the body's major blood passageway.
The Hemopump was commercially released in Germany in February 1996 and has since been released and received rapid acceptance in other European countries, Medtronic said.
